newsitem.title: USA: Foundation gives $200 mln to build Mass. college.
newsitem.headline: Foundation gives $200 mln to build Mass. college.

text.p: A New York City foundation pledged Friday to grant at least $200 million to build a brand-new engineering college outside Boston.
The gift, the largest ever given to a U.S. institution of higher education, will create the Franklin W. Olin College of Engineering, named for the Vermont-born industrialist.

The school's endowment is hoped to be large enough to fund free tuition for students, said Lawrence Milas, president of the F.W. Olin Foundation, created by Olin in 1938 to give building grants to schools.

"One of the greatest pressures on colleges today is costs to students," Milas said in a telephone interview. "If we can remove that as a problem, we'll have a much stronger institution and provide a much better service."

Olin, who founded the diversified manufacturing company Olin Corp., had talked during his lifetime about starting his own college, Milas said. The foundation believed that a new school could offer more innovative programmes than if the money had been donated to an existing institution.

"We saw that there was a real opportunity of expanding the envelope beyond what a lot of institutions are currently doing," Milas said. "Innovation will be a part of its institutional mission and culture."
The college plans to buy 60 to 80 acres of land for the new campus in Needham, Mass., next to Babson College, a top-rated private independent business school.
Babson College President William Glavin said the two schools will share some resources and students will mix "just as if they were all in the same school."
"We could see a lot of mixed projects with engineering and business students," he said.
